data.name: eoir_case_outcomes
data.title: Immigration Court Case Outcomes in Georgia
data.summary: Immigration-court cases filed by Georgia respondents each month, how many ended in a removal order, and how long decisions took; annual county totals by custody status.
data.description: Immigration-court cases with a Georgia address of record, filed October 1997 through 1 August 2026, from the case database the Executive Office for Immigration Review posts monthly and the Deportation Data Project processes to one row per case. Counts of cases filed, cases decided, and decided cases that ended in a removal order, the share of decided cases ordered removed, and the average days from filing to decision, by calendar month of filing, EOIR's recorded sex, custody status, whether the latest hearing was in absentia, and nationality at state level; annual totals by county of record and custody status. The county of record of a detained respondent is the detention center's county.
data.source: Executive Office for Immigration Review — Case database (posted monthly to EOIR's FOIA Library), processed by the Deportation Data Project (CC-0)

data.name: ice_287g_agreements
data.title: ICE 287(g) Agreements with Georgia Agencies
data.summary: 287(g) agreements Georgia sheriffs, police and state agencies signed with ICE each year, and how many were in force, by model and county.
data.description: 287(g) agreements between U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Georgia law-enforcement agencies - the memoranda of agreement under INA section 287(g) that deputize state and local officers to perform immigration-enforcement functions. Counts of agreements signed in each calendar year and of agreements in force at year end, by support model (jail enforcement, task force, warrant service officer, and the 2008-2013 combined jail & task force MOA), statewide and by the signing agency's county, from the Deportation Data Project's reconstruction of every ICE participating-agencies list since 2008 plus ICE and DHS records back to 2002.
data.source: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, via the Deportation Data Project (ice-287g): every archived ICE 287(g) participating-agencies list, resolved into agreement records

data.name: ice_arrests
data.title: ICE Arrests in Georgia
data.summary: Monthly counts of ICE arrests made in Georgia since October 2022 and the share that led to ICE detention, by gender, criminal history, arrest method, and citizenship.
data.description: Count of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) administrative arrests made in Georgia, by calendar year and month, with the number and share of those arrests that led to a stay in ICE detention. Built from the Deportation Data Project's table joining each ICE arrest (person-level records ICE released under FOIA, deduplicated by DDP) to the detention stay it led to, if any. Each arrest is counted once and broken out by ICE's gender determination, criminality at arrest (convicted, pending charges, or other immigration violator), how the arrest was made (at-large, custodial, 287(g) program, other), and country of citizenship. State-level only: the source has no arrest-county field. The detention share is a DDP estimate from an approximate arrest-to-stay match; detention stays that did not begin with an ICE arrest (most border arrests) are out of scope.
data.source: Deportation Data Project — ICE arrests joined to detention stays (ICE records released under FOIA in Hausman v. ICE, deduplicated and matched by DDP)

data.name: ice_detainers
data.title: ICE Detainers Issued to Georgia Jails
data.summary: Detainers ICE sent to Georgia jails each month, how many were declined or honored, and annual totals by the receiving jail's county.
data.description: Immigration detainers ICE issued to jails and prisons in Georgia, October 2022 through 6 August 2026, from the ICE detainer records released under FOIA (Hausman v. ICE) and published by the Deportation Data Project. Most are I-247A detainers asking a jail to hold someone up to 48 hours past release so ICE can take custody; about a fifth are I-247G requests for advance notification of release, which ask for notice rather than a hold. Counts of detainers issued, declined by the receiving agency, and honored (the person booked into ICE detention), by calendar month, ICE's gender determination, criminal history at issuance, the ICE program that issued the detainer, and citizenship country at state level; annual totals by the receiving jail's county.
data.source: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, ERO LESA Statistical Tracking Unit - detainer records released under FOIA (Hausman v. ICE), published unprocessed by the Deportation Data Project

data.name: ice_detention_stays
data.title: ICE Detention Stays at Georgia Facilities
data.summary: ICE detention stays with any time at a Georgia facility: stays begun each month, how long they lasted, how much of that was in Georgia, and how they ended.
data.description: Stays in ICE detention that spent any time at a Georgia facility, October 2022 through 6 August 2026, from the ICE detention records released under FOIA (Hausman v. ICE) and processed to the stay and stint level by the Deportation Data Project. A stay is one uninterrupted period in ICE custody, possibly across several facilities and states; it counts here if at least one of its facility book-ins was in Georgia, and its county is the Georgia county where it spent the most time. Counts of stays begun and ended, the average length of the whole ended stay, the average days of it spent in Georgia, and the average number of facilities per stay, by calendar month, ICE's gender determination, the arresting agency (ICE or CBP), how the stay ended, and citizenship country at state level; annual totals by the facility's county.
data.source: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention records released under FOIA (Hausman v. ICE), processed to one row per detention stay and one row per facility stint by the Deportation Data Project

data.name: ice_detention_stints
data.title: ICE Detention Book-ins at Georgia Facilities
data.summary: Monthly book-ins to ICE detention facilities in Georgia since October 2022, how each stint ended and how long it lasted; annual totals by the facility's county.
data.description: Detention stints - book-ins to one ICE detention facility in Georgia - from 2022-10-01 through 2026-08-06, aggregated from the person-level detention records ICE released under FOIA (Hausman v. ICE) and the Deportation Data Project processed. A stint is time at ONE facility; a person transferred between facilities has several stints, so this is the facility-level view of detention (use ice_detention_stays for people). Counts of stints begun, stints ended, and the mean stint length in days, by calendar month, ICE's gender determination, which agency's arrest led to the detention (ICE or CBP), how the stint ended (transferred, removed, bonded out, paroled, released on order, other, or still detained), and citizenship country at state level; annual totals by the DETENTION FACILITY'S county - Stewart, Charlton (Folkston), Irwin, Fulton and Clayton hold the large facilities, and their rows measure detention capacity, not residents.
data.source: Deportation Data Project - ICE detention stints (ICE detention records released under FOIA in Hausman v. ICE, processed by DDP into one row per facility book-in)

data.name: ice_removals
data.title: ICE Removals Originating in Georgia
data.summary: Monthly counts of deportations (ICE removals) whose originating arrest was recorded in Georgia since October 2022, by ICE program, gender, criminal history, and country of citizenship.
data.description: Count of removals - deportations carried out by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) - whose originating arrest was recorded in Georgia, by calendar year and month of departure, from the person-level removal records ICE released under FOIA (Hausman v. ICE) and the Deportation Data Project published unprocessed. Each removal is counted once and broken out by ICE's gender determination, the case's criminality classification (convicted, pending charges, or other immigration violator), the ICE program that produced the removal (Criminal Alien Program, Fugitive Operations, 287(g), ...), and country of citizenship. State-level only: the source has no county field. Removals with no recorded apprehension state are in no state's count, so this is a floor: linking each removal to the same person's ICE arrest record puts the arrest in Georgia for about 57% more removals (see limitations).
data.source: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, ERO LESA Statistical Tracking Unit - removal records released under FOIA (Hausman v. ICE), published unprocessed by the Deportation Data Project

data.name: naturalizations
data.title: Naturalizations
data.summary: Georgia residents who became U.S. citizens by naturalization each federal fiscal year, with FY2024 country and region of birth.
data.description: Number of people aged 18 and over naturalized as U.S. citizens while living in Georgia, by federal fiscal year, from the DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics (OHSS) Yearbook of Immigration Statistics 2024: Georgia's statewide total FY2015-FY2024 (Table 23) and, for FY2024, the same total broken down by country of birth (26 leading countries, other, unknown) and, separately, by world region of birth (Supplemental Table 1). Rounded by OHSS to the nearest 10.
data.source: DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics (OHSS) - Yearbook of Immigration Statistics 2024, Table 23 and Naturalizations Supplemental Table 1

data.name: new_permanent_residents
data.title: New Lawful Permanent Residents
data.summary: Georgians who became lawful permanent residents (green card) by fiscal year: state totals, and top counties by country and class.
data.description: Number of people who obtained lawful permanent resident (LPR, green card) status while living in Georgia, by federal fiscal year, from the DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics (OHSS). Statewide totals FY2015-FY2024 (Yearbook of Immigration Statistics 2024, Table 4) with separate country-of-birth and world-region-of-birth breakdowns for FY2024 (Supplemental Table 1); and, for the 4-7 Georgia counties among the 200 U.S. counties with the most new LPRs each year, FY2007-FY2024 counts by country of birth and major class of admission (OHSS Top 200 Counties tables). OHSS publishes no county all-country/all-class total; the key metric num_new_lprs_estimated carries a platform estimate there and OHSS's figures (its cells, exact sums of them, or 0 where it lists none) everywhere else; num_new_lprs is the same series without the estimates.
data.source: DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics (OHSS) - New LPRs by State, County, Country of Birth, and Major Class of Admission (Top 200 Counties); Yearbook of Immigration Statistics 2024. County all-country/all-class totals estimated by Georgia Civic Data

data.name: h1b_lca_positions
data.title: H-1B Labor Condition Application Positions
data.summary: H-1B (and H-1B1/E-3) worker positions the Labor Department certified for Georgia worksites each fiscal year, by county, occupation, visa program and outcome.
data.description: Positions certified by the U.S. Department of Labor on labor condition applications (LCAs) for H-1B specialty-occupation workers - and the H-1B1 (Chile, Singapore) and E-3 (Australia) programs that file the same form - at Georgia worksites, by federal fiscal year: the job slots DOL's Office of Foreign Labor Certification (OFLC) certified, with the positions requested and the number of applications decided. Statewide by case outcome, occupation group and visa program, and by the county of the LCA's first worksite. From OFLC's LCA program disclosure data, FY2020 through the third quarter of FY2026. An LCA precedes the H-1B petition and the cap lottery: certified positions are not visas issued or workers hired.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: LCA (H-1B, H-1B1, E-3) program disclosure data (Performance Data), FY2020-FY2026 Q3

data.name: h1b_lca_secondary_worksites
data.title: H-1B LCAs Listing a Georgia Secondary Worksite
data.summary: H-1B (and H-1B1/E-3) labor condition applications certified for jobs based outside Georgia that also list a Georgia worksite, each fiscal year, statewide and by county.
data.description: H-1B labor condition applications (LCAs) - and the H-1B1 (Chile, Singapore) and E-3 (Australia) applications on the same form - that the U.S. Department of Labor certified for a job whose FIRST worksite is outside Georgia but that also list a worksite in Georgia, by federal fiscal year: statewide by occupation group and visa program, and by the county of each listed Georgia worksite. These LCAs are the ones h1b_lca_positions (which counts each LCA at its first worksite) leaves out. From OFLC's LCA disclosure data and annual worksite files, FY2020-FY2025. The count of LCAs is exact; their positions are an upper bound on the positions that may work in Georgia, and a listed worksite is not proof of a hire.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: LCA (H-1B, H-1B1, E-3) program disclosure data and LCA worksite files (Performance Data), FY2020-FY2025

data.name: h1b_wage_offers
data.title: H-1B Wage Offers
data.summary: Median annual wage offered on the H-1B, H-1B1 and E-3 positions the Labor Department certified for Georgia worksites each fiscal year, by county and occupation group.
data.description: The median annual wage employers offered on the specialty-occupation positions (H-1B, H-1B1 Chile/Singapore and E-3 Australia) whose labor condition applications DOL's Office of Foreign Labor Certification certified for Georgia worksites, by federal fiscal year, weighted by positions certified: statewide by occupation group and by the county of the LCA's first worksite, with the positions and LCAs behind each median. The same LCAs as h1b_lca_positions, which counts the positions. From OFLC's LCA program disclosure data, FY2020 through the third quarter of FY2026.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: LCA program (H-1B, H-1B1, E-3) disclosure data (Performance Data), FY2020-FY2026 Q3

data.name: h2a_certifications
data.title: H-2A Agricultural Labor Certifications
data.summary: H-2A temporary farmworker positions the Labor Department certified for Georgia worksites each fiscal year, by county, occupation and outcome.
data.description: Positions certified by the U.S. Department of Labor for H-2A temporary agricultural workers at Georgia worksites, by federal fiscal year: the job slots DOL's Office of Foreign Labor Certification (OFLC) approved on each employer's H-2A application, with the positions requested and the number of applications decided. Statewide by case outcome, occupation (SOC) and whether the employer is an H-2A labor contractor, and by the county of the application's first worksite. From OFLC's H-2A program disclosure data, FY2020 through the third quarter of FY2026.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: H-2A program disclosure data (Performance Data), FY2020-FY2026 Q3

data.name: h2a_wage_offers
data.title: H-2A Wage Offers
data.summary: Average hourly wage offered on the H-2A farmworker positions the Labor Department certified for Georgia worksites each fiscal year, by county and occupation.
data.description: The average hourly wage employers offered on the H-2A temporary agricultural positions DOL's Office of Foreign Labor Certification certified for Georgia worksites, by federal fiscal year, weighted by positions certified: statewide by occupation (SOC) and by the county of the application's first worksite, with the positions and applications behind each average. The same applications as h2a_certifications, which counts the positions. From OFLC's H-2A program disclosure data, FY2020 through the third quarter of FY2026.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: H-2A program disclosure data (Performance Data), FY2020-FY2026 Q3

data.name: h2a_worker_housing
data.title: H-2A Worker Housing
data.summary: Beds, housing units and sites employers listed for H-2A farmworkers in Georgia on certified job orders, by fiscal year and county.
data.description: Housing capacity that employers listed for H-2A temporary agricultural workers at sites in Georgia, by federal fiscal year: the beds (total occupancy), housing units and housing sites on the job orders the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Foreign Labor Certification (OFLC) certified in the year, and the number of those job orders. Statewide and by the county of each housing site, from the primary housing in Section D of each job order and the additional housing in its Addendum B, in OFLC's H-2A program disclosure data, FY2020 through the third quarter of FY2026.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: H-2A program disclosure data (Performance Data), main file Section D housing and Addendum B Housing, FY2020-FY2026 Q3

data.name: h2b_certifications
data.title: H-2B Non-Agricultural Labor Certifications
data.summary: H-2B temporary non-farm worker positions the Labor Department certified for Georgia worksites each fiscal year, by county, occupation, cap status, nature of need and outcome.
data.description: Positions certified by the U.S. Department of Labor for H-2B temporary non-agricultural workers at Georgia worksites, by federal fiscal year: the job slots DOL's Office of Foreign Labor Certification (OFLC) approved on each employer's H-2B application, with the positions requested and the number of applications decided. Statewide by case outcome, occupation (SOC), whether the workers are subject to the H-2B visa cap and the employer's stated nature of the temporary need (seasonal, peakload, one-time occurrence, intermittent), and by the county of the application's first worksite. From OFLC's H-2B program disclosure data, FY2020 through the third quarter of FY2026.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: H-2B program disclosure data (Performance Data), FY2020-FY2026 Q3

data.name: h2b_wage_offers
data.title: H-2B Wage Offers
data.summary: Average hourly wage offered on the H-2B non-farm positions the Labor Department certified for Georgia worksites each fiscal year, by county and occupation.
data.description: The average hourly wage employers offered on the H-2B temporary non-agricultural positions DOL's Office of Foreign Labor Certification certified for Georgia worksites, by federal fiscal year, weighted by positions certified: statewide by occupation (SOC) and by the county of the application's first worksite, with the positions and applications behind each average. The same applications as h2b_certifications, which counts the positions. From OFLC's H-2B program disclosure data, FY2020 through the third quarter of FY2026.
data.source: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Foreign Labor Certification: H-2B program disclosure data (Performance Data), FY2020-FY2026 Q3

data.name: deportation_detainers
data.title: Georgia Prison Inmates with Deportation Detainers
data.summary: Georgia state-prison inmates held with an active ICE deportation detainer on a month-end date, by citizenship country and offense group.
data.description: Inmates in Georgia Department of Corrections custody who hold an active immigration (deportation) detainer, from GDC's monthly 'O.C.G.A. 42-1-11.4 Monthly Report - Detainers for Deportation'. A point-in-time count on the report's as-of date (a month-end), statewide, with the total broken down by the inmate's country of citizenship and, separately, by offense group. Only the months whose report was captured exist; GDC overwrites the report monthly and keeps no archive.
data.source: Georgia Department of Corrections - O.C.G.A. 42-1-11.4 Monthly Report, Detainers for Deportation (earlier months via the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine)

data.name: undocumented_population_characteristics
data.title: Undocumented Immigrant Population Characteristics
data.summary: The Center for Migration Studies' 2024 profile of Georgia's undocumented population by sex, age, birthplace and years in the U.S.
data.description: Characteristics of Georgia's undocumented immigrant population from the Center for Migration Studies of New York (CMS), data year 2024: CMS's modeled estimate of 502,000 broken down, one breakdown at a time, by sex, age bracket, world region of birth, country of birth (31 countries) and years in the United States. For the size of the population and how Pew, MPI, CMS and DHS compare, use undocumented_population_estimates.
data.source: Center for Migration Studies of New York, State and National Data Tool (undocumented population, data year 2024)

data.name: undocumented_population_estimates
data.title: Undocumented Immigrant Population Estimates
data.summary: Four modeled estimates of Georgia's undocumented immigrant population (Pew, MPI, CMS, DHS), 1990-2024, plus ten Georgia counties from MPI.
data.description: Modeled estimates of the undocumented (unauthorized) immigrant population living in Georgia from four independent estimators - Pew Research Center (1990-2023, with a 90% margin of error), the Migration Policy Institute (mid-2023, statewide and ten counties), the Center for Migration Studies of New York (data year 2024) and the DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics (January 1 of 2000 and 2005-2022 except 2021, revised series). One row per estimator and reference year; the estimator is always a filter, never summed.
data.source: Pew Research Center; Migration Policy Institute; Center for Migration Studies of New York; DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics

data.name: refugee_arrivals
data.title: Refugee Arrivals in Georgia by Nationality
data.summary: Refugees resettled in Georgia each federal fiscal year since FY2012, by nationality, from the State Department's arrival reports.
data.description: Refugees resettled in Georgia by nationality, per federal fiscal year, from the U.S. Department of State Refugee Processing Center's 'Refugee Arrivals by State and Nationality' reports: the FY2012-FY2025 year-end reports and the FY2026 fiscal-year-to-date report (2025-10-01 through 2026-08-31). One row per fiscal year and nationality, plus Georgia's total (nationality = 'all').
data.source: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration, Refugee Processing Center - Refugee Arrivals by State and Nationality (fiscal-year reports); analyzed by Georgia Civic Data

data.name: refugee_arrivals_monthly
data.title: Monthly Refugee Arrivals in Georgia by Nationality
data.summary: Refugees resettled in Georgia each calendar month since October 2020, by nationality, from the State Department's arrival reports.
data.description: Refugees resettled in Georgia by calendar month of admission and nationality, October 2020 through August 2026, from the U.S. Department of State Refugee Processing Center's 'Refugee Arrivals by State and Nationality' reports (FY2021-FY2025 year-end and FY2026 year to date). One row per calendar month and nationality, plus Georgia's total (nationality = 'all') and calendar-year totals (month = 'all').
data.source: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration, Refugee Processing Center - Refugee Arrivals by State and Nationality (fiscal-year reports, by month of admission); analyzed by Georgia Civic Data

data.name: daca_recipients
data.title: Active DACA Recipients in Georgia
data.summary: Georgia residents holding an active DACA grant, as counted by USCIS on irregular release dates from September 2017 to April 2019 and at federal fiscal quarter-ends since; FY2018 q1 and FY2023 q3 have no release.
data.description: Number of Georgia residents holding Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) on each snapshot date, from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services' Active DACA Recipients reports: the Georgia row of the State or Territory of Residence table, one row per federal fiscal quarter with a release, from FY2017 q4 (as of 2017-09-04) to FY2026 q3 (as of 2026-06-30); FY2018 q1 and FY2023 q3 have no release. Before June 2019 USCIS released at irregular month-ends, each placed in the fiscal quarter containing it. A point-in-time stock, rounded by USCIS to the nearest 10.
data.source: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) - Active DACA Recipients reports, Immigration and Citizenship Data
